terra.problem: The text says the people wept all night, not that their grumbling had been simmering all night.
The text does not say they spoke loudly enough for everybody to hear.
The text does not say nobody asked Moses for his opinion.
The text does not establish that nobody wanted more exploring.
The claim that Joshua and Caleb saw the same hills and walked the same ground as the other spies adds details the text does not give.
Moses and Aaron fell facedown earlier, but the text does not say they were still facedown when Joshua and Caleb spoke.
The imagined rocks and 'Tough crowd' make a joke of the threat to stone Joshua and Caleb.
The LORD asks how long the people will refuse to believe despite the signs. The explanation changes this to a question about why the signs were not enough.
The explanation is generic and ends by simply repeating the answer without adding a natural Papa Dorin voice.
Moses and Aaron are told what to say, but the passage does not establish that the people hear it from both of them. It later says Moses relayed the words.
Saying everyone counted who was twenty or older will fall in the wilderness overlooks the stated exceptions of Caleb and Joshua.
The explanation is a generic restatement of the verse, ending by simply repeating the answer.
The passage does not establish that the LORD gave the direction to turn back on the day before the people went up.
Moses warned that the LORD was not among them; he did not say that he and the ark would remain in the camp. The explanation treats those as the same warning.
